integration: Pass unique track IDs and stable title, artist, album and duration records. onSelect drives the host selection or player.
Like, queue and removal actions are separate sibling controls; omit callbacks to hide actions the host does not support.
Optional host artwork should be licensed and served reliably. The default cover studies are original, offline-safe illustrations.

block-music-workspace.useWhen: Composing a full listening application with discovery, a searchable collection, a shared queue and persistent playback.
block-music-workspace.avoidWhen: Copying a streaming service brand or publishing an audio catalogue without rights to its media and artwork.
integration: Supply MusicTrack records with licensed src URLs. Selection and playback remain distinct and actual media events govern playing state.
Persist queue and liked-state changes through host observers. Retained views keep the collection, search and player position intact.
The offline demo uses fictional releases and original 12-second audio; it begins muted. Production integrations own licensed assets.

collab-message-list.useWhen: Showing a readable team conversation with reply affordances, reversible reactions and respectful arrival of new posts.
collab-message-list.avoidWhen: Treating a visual conversation as a transport layer or asserting delivery before a host returns an authoritative message.
integration: Pass stable message IDs and author identities. Drive reactions and thread navigation through host callbacks.
The viewport follows own posts and preserves earlier reading positions for incoming posts.
Animate reaction figures in both directions; live announcements apply to added messages rather than every count frame.

block-team-workspace.useWhen: Composing channels and direct-message rooms with persistent drafts, an asynchronous send contract and retained threads.
block-team-workspace.avoidWhen: Publishing a communication application without supplying its transport, user identity and persistence requirements.
integration: Supply channels, people and initialMessages with stable IDs. onSend returns the server’s authoritative channel-scoped message.
Channel drafts and opened threads remain mounted. A late response never clears text edited during the request.
Reactions and thread interactions are session state in the example; hosts own durable storage and realtime transport.

collab-call-stage.useWhen: Presenting real participant video streams with camera-off fallbacks, a spotlight layout and clear host-owned media controls.
collab-call-stage.avoidWhen: Using placeholder portraits or animation to claim a live media connection, active speaker or hardware permission.
integration: Supply participant streams from your own session transport. The stage never acquires a camera or microphone by itself.
Use CallControls separately when controls must remain visible across other application views.
Only supply captions and activeSpeakerId when the host has real data. The host owns track lifetimes and audio routing.

block-meetings-workspace.useWhen: Composing a working meeting application with linked agenda context, persistent room controls and independently retained notes.
block-meetings-workspace.avoidWhen: Treating an interface block as a conferencing transport or declaring a room joined before the host acknowledges it.
integration: Supply agenda days, participant streams and join/leave callbacks. Keep selected meeting separate from the joined session.
Media callbacks resolve after host state changes succeed; failures preserve the previous control state.
Notes remain scoped by meeting ID. Hosts own storage, permissions and transport; the offline room uses fictional, camera-off participants.

button-shimmer-track.useWhen: A primary async action needs clear pending, completed and retry states, with a restrained moving edge around the button.
button-shimmer-track.avoidWhen: Repeated immediate actions, or an effect being used as the only indication that an action is available or has succeeded.
integration: Connect the action to a real awaited operation and provide useful failure text.
Keep controlled status synchronized with the host and reset it when starting a new task.
Preserve the native button label and focus treatment when changing colours or motion.

cards-prismatic-folder.useWhen: A compact file collection benefits from a physical folder presentation, readable previews and clear availability states.
cards-prismatic-folder.avoidWhen: Large directory trees, bulk file administration or workflows that need a full file browser.
integration: Supply stable file identifiers and the actual collection status rather than relying on demo content.
Connect file actions and recovery to the host application; the presentation does not fetch or store files.
Review empty collections, unavailable files and long file names in the intended container.

navigation-context-rail.useWhen: A workspace has grouped destinations and needs remembered section context, search and a compact navigation drawer.
navigation-context-rail.avoidWhen: A simple page with one short navigation list, or navigation whose destination content should live inside the rail itself.
integration: Use stable section and item identifiers, with useful reasons for disabled destinations.
Connect navigation to the host router or destination loader and update controlled selection after success.
Provide loading and recovery states, then review narrow containers and focus returning from the drawer.

effect-border-tracer.useWhen: An existing card or control needs a subtle perimeter accent that can follow hover and focus or move continuously while visible.
effect-border-tracer.avoidWhen: Dense reading surfaces, or a moving edge being used as the only focus or status indicator.
integration: Wrap actual host content and keep its controls, labels and action handlers responsible for product behaviour.
Choose the trigger and corner radius to match the host container.
Retain visible focus outlines and review menus extending outside the wrapper, including reduced-motion presentation.

input-detent-dial.useWhen: A bounded numeric setting benefits from tactile, stepped adjustment and a clear indication of the current value.
input-detent-dial.avoidWhen: Unbounded quantities, or a form where a conventional number field with simple step buttons already fits the workflow.
integration: Bind the value and its change handler to the actual setting in the host application.
Choose valid limits and step increments for the domain, and keep the visible value understandable.
Review keyboard adjustment, larger labels and pointer interaction before using the dial as the main control.

devtools-icon-workbench.useWhen: A developer or design workflow needs searchable icon selection, construction previews and SVG or JSX output.
devtools-icon-workbench.avoidWhen: A static icon display, or a workflow that requires an external icon catalogue and assets not supplied by the host.
integration: Supply the intended icon set and keep controlled selection synchronized with the host.
Choose size and stroke settings appropriate to the destination interface.
Connect custom copy handling when needed and keep clipboard failures visible and recoverable.

navigation-lens-dock.useWhen: A compact set of workspace tools benefits from a dock with clear selection and pointer-based magnification.
navigation-lens-dock.avoidWhen: Large hierarchical navigation, or navigation that depends on magnification to make labels or targets usable.
integration: Provide stable tool identifiers, accessible labels and reasons for disabled items.
Connect activation to real host navigation and update controlled selection after success.
Review keyboard use and static touch or reduced-motion presentation, including recovery from failed activation.

hero-signal-workbench.useWhen: A product introduction benefits from an interactive waveform demonstration with understandable shape, frequency and gain controls.
hero-signal-workbench.avoidWhen: A product whose value has no useful relationship to a signal demonstration, or a claim that the illustration supplies an audio engine.
integration: Replace introductory copy and supply the intended primary-action destination.
Connect controlled parameters and change handling to the host if the demonstration needs shared state.
Keep the parameter labels and output understandable; the component does not make audio or network requests.

navigation-stacked-tabs.useWhen: Several documents share one working area and people need to reorder, close and restore tabs while preserving unsaved state.
navigation-stacked-tabs.avoidWhen: A short set of fixed product sections, where an ordinary tab bar is easier to scan and does not need document lifecycle controls.
integration: Keep stable document IDs and distinguish dirty changes from acknowledged saves.
The host owns document contents and closure decisions; preserve drafts when a close request is rejected.
Treat items as authoritative document availability. Removing a model retires its open tab, retained panel and closed history; keep it available while restoration is allowed.

layout-split-resizer.useWhen: Two related views need adjustable space, such as an editor beside a preview or a record list beside its details.
layout-split-resizer.avoidWhen: Independent page sections that should stack and scroll naturally, or a split whose minimum usable widths cannot fit the available container.
integration: Set meaningful minimum pane sizes and provide content that remains usable at each supported size.
Persist the chosen split in the host when needed; keyboard resizing and collapse should preserve a useful restoration size.
Use orientation="auto" to stack in narrow containers. A requested percentage is a preference; onPaneSizesChange reports bounded visible percentages and logical pixel sizes.
Keep the host panes mounted when retaining editor drafts, and provide usable scrolling when supplied minimum sizes cannot fit.

media-device-switcher.useWhen: A responsive product demonstration that needs actual phone, tablet and desktop content widths.
media-device-switcher.avoidWhen: A browser emulator, operating-system simulator or screenshot-only carousel.
integration: Supply content that responds to its own container width. The frame selection reports a viewing preference and does not emulate native operating-system behavior.
Keep device labels, dimensions and initial selection explicit; use separate content only when the underlying experience truly differs.

media-image-contact-sheet.useWhen: Reviewing a supplied image collection, making an explicit selection and comparing two or more selected images in the same contact sheet.
media-image-contact-sheet.avoidWhen: Full-size zooming, pixel editing or autoplaying a promotional image carousel.
integration: Supply stable image IDs, real sources and descriptive alternative text. Empty images and empty selection are separate states; expose collection loading and host errors honestly.

Pair controlled selection, query and comparison with their corresponding observers; without one, that branch is read-only. Rejected requests keep actual values, and per-image retry receives an AbortSignal so retired assets cannot replace current results.

media-focus-lightbox.useWhen: An image inspection task that benefits from focused zoom, pan and previous or next navigation.
media-focus-lightbox.avoidWhen: A text document viewer, a video player or a decorative modal that contains no inspectable media.
integration: Supply image sources with meaningful descriptions and stable IDs. Keep the trigger available so closing the viewer can restore logical focus.
Zoom and pan remain bounded to the visible image; use keyboard and static-view controls where a gesture is unavailable.

media-trim-timeline.useWhen: Choosing an exact in/out range from real audio, using a supplied measured waveform alongside precise time entry.
media-trim-timeline.avoidWhen: Encoding an audio file without a host export service, inspecting a video filmstrip or showing a decorative scrubber.
integration: Supply a real source and measured waveform data when available. Native duration defines the trim bounds; keyboard steps and exact time entry serve different precision needs.
Use onApplyRange with its AbortSignal for host processing. Real playback follows native media events, and rejected controlled ranges must remain visibly unchanged.

media-spatial-collection.useWhen: Browsing a small collection of albums or related media objects with visible depth and an equally usable readable list.
media-spatial-collection.avoidWhen: Playing media, presenting a huge sortable data collection or hiding important labels behind overlapping covers.
integration: Supply stable collection IDs, titles, creators and the real entries each object contains. Provide artwork when available and preserve truthful missing or failed cover states.

Keep selected collection and spatial/list view controlled only when the host accepts those requests. Use the optional opening callback and its AbortSignal for a real host action; reduced motion keeps useful static poses.

media-transcript-player.useWhen: Listening to supplied media while reading timed passages and seeking directly from the transcript.
media-transcript-player.avoidWhen: A transcription service, an automatic caption generator or text that has no timing relationship to the supplied recording.
integration: Supply actual playable media and timed transcript segments. Treat gaps, unavailable playback and invalid timing as honest states.
Keep transcript reading and selected passages available even when the media cannot play; synchronize against the real media clock.

media-compare-grid.useWhen: Inspecting several supplied visual variants with coordinated zoom and pan.
media-compare-grid.avoidWhen: A simple before-and-after wipe or a data table that compares textual values.
integration: Supply stable variant IDs, labels and real image sources. One atomic view state contains active image, linked policy and the per-image cameras; link normalized coordinates only for meaningfully comparable framing.

Pair value/defaultValue with onValueChange and observe completed accepted gestures through onValueCommit. Rejected requests preserve actual cameras; keyboard controls, reset and Escape recovery make inspection usable without pointer dragging.

portfolio-project-reel.useWhen: Presenting a focused set of supplied projects with a large visual and readable case notes, using deliberate previous/next navigation.
portfolio-project-reel.avoidWhen: A dense component catalogue, a continuous decorative marquee or an autoplay-only sales presentation.
integration: Supply stable project IDs, titles, summaries and optional artwork, native image sources or actual case-study destinations. Absent links stay absent, and image loading is reported honestly.
Control selection with value/onValueChange when needed. The finite index, keyboard controls and touch swipes preserve readable notes, focus and measured container height while projects change.

media-crop-workbench.useWhen: Framing a supplied image precisely with a real crop preview, ratio presets and matching normalized and pixel coordinates.
media-crop-workbench.avoidWhen: Retouching, removing a background or claiming an encoded export when the host has not provided processing.
integration: Provide a stable image ID, source and alternative text. Actual native dimensions determine pixels; the controlled box is normalized and rejected changes must not commit.

Handle onApply(payload, AbortSignal) with real processing and return a downloadable result only when available. The offline demo creates a Canvas PNG; live selection or image changes retire stale processing and download links.

media-caption-styler.useWhen: Tuning supplied caption text against footage or a still with safe-area and readability guides.
media-caption-styler.avoidWhen: A speech transcription service, an automatic subtitle translator or a complete video export engine.
integration: Supply caption text and the visual context being reviewed. Match the configurable frame aspect ratio to the actual output, including portrait footage; the saved style uses a 1080 px reference width.
Expose wrapping, size and safe-area controls without relying on hover. Missing footage should preserve a useful text and style preview.

hero-layout-playground.useWhen: Demonstrating how actual supplied content reflows as a continuous layout boundary changes.
hero-layout-playground.avoidWhen: Switching between fixed device presets or pretending to emulate a browser or operating system.
integration: Supply real React content that responds to its own container. Pointer, keyboard and precise width requests should describe the same constraint without remounting the content.
Keep requested width distinct from measured available width when the host is narrower. Controlled rejection and unavailable content must remain honest.

features-integration-trace.useWhen: Explaining a supplied integration by following its data through inspectable transformation stages.
features-integration-trace.avoidWhen: A decorative logo cloud, a general workflow editor or a claim of a live integration without host evidence.
integration: Supply stable integration and stage IDs, typed JSON input/output examples and actual availability. The offline demonstration computes its examples locally and does not claim to execute an external integration.
Control selection as an integration/stage pair when the host owns it. Retry receives an AbortSignal, and real clipboard failure needs an actionable copy fallback.

features-shortcut-theatre.useWhen: Demonstrating a product action through explicit, accessible shortcut controls and a supplied live preview.
features-shortcut-theatre.avoidWhen: Registering global shortcuts without consent or animating a keyboard that performs no useful action.
integration: Supply the demonstrated action and clear shortcut labels. Pointer, touch and keyboard controls should invoke the same bounded preview operation.
Keep unavailable actions explainable, respect host rejection and avoid intercepting ordinary typing in adjacent fields.

features-compare-lenses.useWhen: Comparing two supplied approaches to the same workflow using corresponding, inspectable stages.
features-compare-lenses.avoidWhen: A before/after image wipe or unsupported claims that one product is faster or better.
integration: Supply comparable stages and concrete differences. Keep timings and outcomes tied to the host evidence rather than invented numbers.
Let readers select stages and retain readable context on narrow containers; linked navigation should remain optional when the workflows differ.

pricing-usage-calculator.useWhen: Estimating usage charges from explicit supplied rates, included units and bounded quantities.
pricing-usage-calculator.avoidWhen: A checkout flow, an undisclosed pricing formula or a promise that an estimate is the final invoice.
integration: Supply integer minor currency-unit base and block rates, included units, block size and an explicit started-block or proportional-ceiling rounding policy. Intl supplies currency minor-unit precision; missing, invalid or overflowing terms remain unavailable.

Pair a controlled quantity with onQuantityChange. Whole pointer and exact quantities are retained even when they do not align with the keyboard step; host updates synchronize untouched fields and preserve dirty drafts until acceptance or Escape. Checkout remains a separate explicit action.

pricing-seat-simulator.useWhen: Exploring a transparent bill for mixed seat types and billing terms before purchase.
pricing-seat-simulator.avoidWhen: Automatically assigning seats, changing a subscription or concealing discounts inside a single unexplained total.
integration: Supply stable roles, bounded whole counts and integer minor-unit monthly or annual full-term prices. Missing role counts use each supplied minimum. Annual prices represent the complete year, not a disguised monthly amount. Duplicate or empty role IDs invalidate the bill; invalid alternative terms are visibly unavailable and excluded from keyboard selection.

Control term and counts atomically through value/onValueChange. Preserve seat counts when terms change, retain dirty exact-entry drafts through host updates or unavailable rates, and reject invalid or overflowing mixes before any host-owned purchase action.

social-proof-case-ledger.useWhen: Presenting supplied case outcomes together with their measurement period and supporting evidence.
social-proof-case-ledger.avoidWhen: Invented customer statistics, unsupported endorsements or a decorative testimonial carousel.
integration: Supply stable records with actual baseline/follow-up observations, period, sample, methodology and supporting excerpts or real source links. Missing or nonfinite observations remain unavailable; percentage changes use a nonzero absolute baseline denominator.

Keep record navigation separate from native evidence disclosure. Retain the selected record after rejected changes, preserve outside focus and make unknown records, absent measurements and missing evidence readable rather than inventing values.

content-interactive-spec.useWhen: Exploring a product specification through selectable annotations on a supplied diagram.
content-interactive-spec.avoidWhen: A CAD editor, a decorative image hotspot or an unsupported claim about an actual product.
integration: Supply static drawing content, its actual aspect ratio and stable parts with normalized physical coordinates, exact detail fields and real optional references. Invalid positions stay available through the equivalent parts list; artwork is inert.

Use physical directional keys for spatial targets and reading-order keys for the list. Touch targets retain safe margins, controlled rejection retains the actual ring/annotation, and live reduced motion stops coordinate and height owners immediately.

cta-project-brief.useWhen: Collecting a concise project brief and presenting a review before an explicit host-owned submission.
cta-project-brief.avoidWhen: Submitting automatically, fabricating delivery confirmation or hiding a long sales questionnaire inside a small CTA.
integration: Supply an exact name/email/project/details draft, the validation minimum and an acknowledged onSubmit(snapshot, AbortSignal) handler. Review preserves the exact entered text and failure or cancellation retains it.

Retire pending requests when text, handler, availability, validation or reset identity changes. A missing handler renders a review without a fake send action; the original offline demo retains its receipt only in preview memory.

footer-sitemap-atlas.useWhen: Offering a useful grouped site index with real destinations in a compact footer.
footer-sitemap-atlas.avoidWhen: A full application command palette or decorative navigation labels with no destination.
integration: Supply actual site/brand/copyright and groups with stable IDs, real optional URLs and availability reasons. currentHref marks an exact destination; the component never invents routes or executes navigation while expanding.

Exact query/onQueryChange and openGroups/onOpenGroupsChange pairs are independently controlled. Rejected changes preserve the actual result set/disclosures. Local defaults are seeds; resetKey explicitly resets them. Matching is accent/case insensitive against supplied labels and descriptions.

Below700px of actual container width, groups become44px disclosures with inert closed links. Search reveals matches without mutating saved compact expansion. Measure actual content height; live reduced motion stops/sets height and count owners. Retired/disabled links recover only owned focus, while a primary outside-background click clears memory.

text-optical-weight.useWhen: Inspecting how supported font weight and optical scale change real, selectable specimen text.
text-optical-weight.avoidWhen: Synthesizing unsupported font axes or using a font specimen as a decorative loading animation.
integration: Supply selectable specimen copy and a font role backed by your actual CSS font. The bundled Geist Variable display/mono roles declare weight100–900; Instrument Serif is fixed400. Optical size remains undeclared unless the host font actually supports its supplied optical axis.

Control weight, requested size and any declared optical size atomically. Keep exact controls keyboard accessible, report requested versus fitted rendered size and retain actual values after rejected changes.

text-path-typesetter.useWhen: Placing supplied text along a bounded curve while inspecting actual spacing and readable text content.
text-path-typesetter.avoidWhen: A full vector drawing tool or turning essential body copy into an inaccessible decorative outline.
integration: Supply a quadratic curve with actual dimensions and start/control/end coordinates, selectable text and a real font role. Bend is a bounded delta from the supplied control point; zero preserves the supplied geometry.

Control font size, spacing, offset and bend atomically. Inspect actual native SVG path/glyph bounds, report curve overrun or viewport clipping, and preserve a readable linear equivalent and unique SVG IDs for multiple instances.

text-number-odometer.useWhen: Presenting changing numeric values with interruptible rolls for increases, decreases, signs and decimals.
text-number-odometer.avoidWhen: A static counter, falsely precise analytics or animation that obscures the final accessible value.
integration: Supply the actual finite value and explicit fractionDigits (0–6), locale, grouping and signDisplay. Prefix/suffix are literal supplied text, not currency or unit conversion. The first render is already the actual formatted value.

Retarget each decorative digit from its current glyph phase on interrupted increases, decreases and sign/decimal changes. Invalid configuration and nonfinite values retain readable recovery; native font metrics fit actual numerals to the container and preserve exact selection.

Live reduced motion stops and sets every owner. Accessible final text stays separate from hidden rolling glyphs; opt into live only when a polite final-value announcement is useful. Use the named output in host controls rather than inventing additional counters.

text-outline-fill.useWhen: Connecting a readable outlined text treatment to supplied reading progress.
text-outline-fill.avoidWhen: Essential copy that only becomes legible after scrolling or an uncontrolled looping text effect.
integration: Supply the text and bounded progress or a real progress source. Keep a fully readable static layer and preserve ordinary text selection.
Honor reduced motion and missing progress without hiding words; visual fill must not imply that a user actually completed the content.

bg-fluted-glass.useWhen: Separating supplied foreground content from a layered scene with a restrained fluted refraction treatment.
bg-fluted-glass.avoidWhen: Making text less legible, imitating unsupported live refraction or adding expensive animation behind every panel.
integration: Supply a real scene image and independent foreground children. The surface applies SVG displacement to the supplied image; it does not capture or refract a live backdrop. Preserve foreground interaction, selectable content and intentional overflow.

Use strength0–32 and frost0–2.5 in host CSS pixels, integer flutes8–40, vertical/horizontal orientation and radius0–64. Standard/high quality bounds the decorative scene to 640,000/1,280,000 layout pixels. Scale only that scene and normalize filter strength to host coordinates.

Use actual native Image load/decode dimensions and scoped onSceneStateChange receipts. Source replacement retires old image results, retry operates on the real current source, and unavailable content stays clear. Static displacement has no ambient loop to pause; preserve the same readable foreground under reduced motion.

bg-topographic-contours.useWhen: Exploring a controlled contour surface by changing bounded density and lighting inputs.
bg-topographic-contours.avoidWhen: A geographic map, live terrain analysis or an endlessly drifting background with no controls.
integration: Supply a finite exact scalar grid with columns/rows2–48 and columns×rows values, independent foreground children and actual availability. Marching squares draws real iso-levels from the supplied range. The original32×24 default is synthetic artwork, not geographic data.

Integer density8–24 interpolates actual levels; lightAngle 0–359 takes the shortest arc during real changes. Standard/high quality caps backing pixels at 640,000/1,280,000 independently of DPR. Reuse crossing buffers and cached paths for light-only changes; do not rasterize foreground content.

Validate actual content revisions even when the field object/array identity is reused. There is no idle/offscreen animation loop. Stop/set decorative transition owners under live reduced motion, preserve foreground interaction/overflow and make invalid/loading/error states explicit.

pixel-halftone-image.useWhen: Inspecting a supplied image as a real halftone pattern with useful density and threshold adjustments.
pixel-halftone-image.avoidWhen: Stock-image decoration, background removal or claiming an encoded export without an actual output.
integration: Provide a stable source ID, actual image URL, alternative description and optional title. Native decoding and real pixel access determine readiness; cross-origin failures retain an honestly labeled original when ordinary image access succeeds.

Control one atomic spacing/threshold value: whole-pixel spacing 6–20 and threshold 0.10–1.00 in0.01 steps. Missing controlled handlers make editing read-only. Requests preserve host authority, and only accepted completed changes reach onValueCommit.

Original comparison fits the complete source. Actual sampling/output pixels are bounded to 640,000 standard or 1,280,000 high, max 4096px per side. onExport receives a real PNG Blob, output dimensions, source ID and accepted settings with AbortSignal. The PNG is the bounded view raster, not a claim of full source resolution; saving/downloading belongs to the host.

Keep the accepted settings and focus through export failure. Source/settings/handler revisions abort old work and ignore late settlement. Live reduced motion stops actual decorative owners; parent-page focus remains owned by the parent.

effect-ink-trail.useWhen: Adding a bounded, user-driven drawing mark that fades while ordinary controls remain usable.
effect-ink-trail.avoidWhen: Capturing the whole page pointer, hiding essential content or creating an endless uncontrolled animation.
integration: Keep drawing inside its dedicated bounded surface. Ordinary foreground overlays are separate from drawing disabled semantics and retain native input, touch, events, accessibility and overflow. Keyboard arrows move the drawing marker; Space/Enter or Stamp mark creates the same actual mark.

Omitted ink follows the current theme; an explicit six-digit color stays authoritative. onStroke reports completed normalized points with actual pressure/time and snapshotted width, color and lifetime. Host persistence is explicit. Pointer cancellation, Escape, resetKey, disabled and hidden state retire owned gestures; retained marks are bounded to 24 with 1024 points per stroke.

New marks fade after release over 300–3000ms. Live reduced motion freezes current opacity until clear, and normal motion resumes from that pose. Main Canvas pixels are capped at 640,000 with max 4096px per side. Idle/offscreen work stops. Bound any host overlay intentionally; the offline demo alone bounds its editable note resize to the actual drawing height.

three-material-inspector.useWhen: Comparing generic material samples under explicit, adjustable light in a small 3D inspection tool.
three-material-inspector.avoidWhen: Replacing an actual product photograph with a generated stand-in or making unsupported physical material claims.
integration: Supply 1–8 raw unique material IDs with labels/descriptions, hex color and bounded appearance parameters: metalness 0–1, roughness 0.15–1, transmission 0–0.8. The original generic coupon is illustrative; use real assets for actual products or calibrated material work.

One atomic value owns materialId, whole-degree azimuth −90–90 and lightAngle 0–359. Native radios/ranges, scaled pointer turning and keyboard arrows share host requests; rejected controlled values never create false commits. Unknown identities remain explicit, and absent controlled handlers make editing read-only.

Standard/high quality bounds the main drawing buffer to 480,000/960,000 pixels with max 2048px side; auxiliary environment/shadow/transmission targets are separately bounded. Data revisions prepare their own native context and ignore retired readiness. Label/description edits retain the context.

Keep the useful diagram and actual appearance parameters when graphics are unavailable, with explicit retry. Idle/hidden rendering stops, live reduced motion settles real owners, and owner-document focus fencing preserves native parent actions.

three-exploded-assembly.useWhen: Inspecting labeled parts of a generic supplied assembly through an explicit exploded view and diagram alternative.
three-exploded-assembly.avoidWhen: Engineering certification, accurate manufacturing CAD or a product visualization based on invented geometry.
integration: Supply 1–12 raw unique labeled parametric box/cylinder/frame pieces with actual size, position, explosion vector and hex color. Dimensions are 0.05–6 model units, positions within ±8, vectors within ±4. Units are illustrative; the component is not a manufacturing CAD or imported-model viewer.

Control one atomic selectedId/null, separation 0–1 in0.01 steps and whole-degree azimuth −75–75. Real geometry selection and the complete native parts list share requests; rejected changes retain the accepted pose. Unknown identities never choose a fallback, and Reset pose is explicit.

Keep readable part names/notes and the schematic available without graphics. Standard/high main-buffer caps are 400,000/800,000 pixels, max 2048px side, with a separately bounded 512px shadow target. Data revisions own their actual native readiness, while copy edits retain their context.

Native bounded dragging, keyboard ranges and Escape preserve host authority. Live reduced motion settles actual pose owners, hidden/idle rendering stops, resources are retired on unmount and parent-page focus stays with the parent.

input-dual-range.useWhen: Choosing a bounded interval with two handles and precise numeric endpoints.
input-dual-range.avoidWhen: A single-value slider or a timeline that also needs actual media playback.
integration: Supply one atomic lower/upper pair with finite ordered min/max, equally spaced step, whole-step minimumGap and clamp/push collision policy. Domains support up to six decimal places and100,000 steps within ±1,000,000. Invalid configuration or out-of-domain host values stays explicit; repairing is a requested minimum interval, never automatic coercion.

Native lower/upper handles and exact decimal fields share the same accepted pair. Exact drafts follow host authority until actually edited, preserve newer revisions through older acknowledgements and remain visible when controlled callbacks reject a request. Absent controlled handlers lock editing; resetKey explicitly resets local seeds.

The ruler band and tabular interval/width figures move in both directions from current visible state. Live reduced motion stops/sets every owner. Provide native touch/keyboard handles, readable limits and minimum gap, actual focus rings, and primary outside-background ownership guards.

input-unit-converter.useWhen: Changing display units while preserving one underlying physical quantity and explicit precision.
input-unit-converter.avoidWhen: Currency exchange with stale rates or silently changing the underlying value when the display unit changes.
integration: Supply unique nonempty units with positive finite factor and finite offset, plus one canonical base/unitId pair. Display=base×factor+offset. Changing unit requests the unchanged base, never a rounded inverse; canonicalUnit is the actual underlying unit label.

Precision0–6 controls display/edit digits. Mark a rounded display explicitly, show canonical limits and preserve untouched authority. Dirty drafts retain their original unit definition when view units change; changed/removed definitions block stale application. Rejected requests and older acknowledgements preserve newer edits.

Use exact controlled value/onValueChange or local seeds/resetKey. Within an unchanged conversion definition, figures retarget up/down; new definitions show one actual entry value rather than fabricated intermediate units. Live reduced motion stops owners, native controls keep focus, and absent controlled handlers lock editing.

input-cron-builder.useWhen: Composing a supported recurring schedule and inspecting actual upcoming occurrences in a supplied timezone.
input-cron-builder.avoidWhen: Accepting arbitrary scheduler syntax or promising execution when no host scheduler exists.
integration: Use CronSchedule: daily or weekly cadence, HH:mm local time, unique weekdays (Sunday0–Saturday6), actual supplied timeZone and first/second repeatedTime. The five-field cron string is exported separately from its time-zone and daylight-saving policies.

Pass a real Gregorian ISO referenceInstant with explicit Z or offset (1970–2100) and1–12 occurrences. The preview skips missing local times and resolves the chosen repeated occurrence, within a100-day horizon. The default reference is a visible fixed example.

Explicit Apply requests a cloned complete schedule through onValueChange. Controlled rejection keeps the accepted schedule and draft; an older acknowledgement cannot replace a newer edit. Local values reset through resetKey.

Copy uses actual Clipboard API success and produces cron,timeZone,repeatedTime and missingTime:skip. Configure your scheduler with matching policies; the component does not execute or persist schedules.

input-expression-editor.useWhen: Editing a small, explicitly supported expression with syntax feedback and a transparent computed example.
input-expression-editor.avoidWhen: Evaluating arbitrary JavaScript or implying support for a complete programming language.
integration: Supply at most32 unique ExpressionField identifiers with a declared number, text or boolean kind and optional matching finite example. The parser accepts at most512 characters,128 tokens and32 nested operations. It never uses eval or accepts arbitrary JavaScript.

Supported syntax: decimal numbers, escaped quoted text, true/false, fields, parentheses, unary + / − / !, numeric + / − / * / /, numeric comparisons, same-type == / != and short-circuit && / ||. Missing examples, division by zero and non-finite or over-±1e12 results remain explicit.

The native textarea retains a separate unapplied draft; fields insert at its real selection. Control+Space inserts the first field, Control/Command+Enter requests Apply, and Escape returns to the accepted expression. Numeric display also exposes the exact computed JS number.

Explicit onValueChange requests the exact valid expression only when its supplied example can be computed. Controlled rejection preserves current expression and draft; an older acknowledgement cannot erase a newer edit. Local seeds change only through resetKey.

selects-tree-picker.useWhen: Selecting hierarchical items with indeterminate parents, search and explainable disabled branches.
selects-tree-picker.avoidWhen: A flat select, a general file browser or bulk selection that ignores unavailable descendants.
integration: Supply unique nonempty PickerNode identities/labels, at most128 items and eight hierarchy levels. Parent disabled state and its explanation propagate to descendants; duplicate identities make selection unavailable.

value is a leaf-identity array; onValueChange receives a cloned atomic request. Group checkboxes include all eligible descendant leaves, including items outside the search. Existing unavailable selections remain visible and retained. Clear selectable items preserves unavailable choices.

query/onQueryChange and expandedIds/onExpandedIdsChange are separately controlled. Accent/case-normalized search temporarily reveals matches and context without replacing stored expansion or selection; clearing it restores actual disclosure choices. Missing controlled handlers produce honest fixed controls.

Native indeterminate checkboxes have separate disclosure actions. Arrow keys visit actual visible targets, Home/End reveal endpoints and logical horizontal keys follow RTL. Folded content is inert; focus recovers only while the component still owns it.

date-range-calendar.useWhen: Choosing a two-ended calendar range with readable bounds and keyboard date navigation.
date-range-calendar.avoidWhen: A time-slot booking system or converting date-only selections through an unintended timezone.
integration: Supply controlled `value` or local `defaultValue` as `{start,end}` real YYYY-MM-DD endpoints, with `onValueChange`. Date-only arithmetic uses Gregorian UTC and never turns a date into an unintended local instant. Missing controlled callbacks make the corresponding range or month actions read only.

Configure inclusive `minDate`/`maxDate`, unique `unavailableDates`, `minimumDays`/`maximumDays` and `weekStartsOn`. Completed ranges must satisfy every unavailable day and inclusive length rule; rejected ranges retain the current endpoint.

Use separately controlled `month`/`onMonthChange` or local `initialMonth`; `resetKey` explicitly resets local range/month context. Keyboard month requests only move focus after the host accepts that actual month and while the original widget-owned intent remains current.

date-timezone-overlap.useWhen: Comparing supplied working hours across timezones before explicitly choosing a meeting time.
date-timezone-overlap.avoidWhen: A guessed timezone offset, a scheduling service or a guarantee that participants are available.
integration: Supply actual YYYY-MM-DD `date`, Intl `anchorZone`, local `windowStart`/`windowEnd` and unique `participants` with local `start`/`end`, `timeZone` and Sunday0–Saturday6 `weekdays`. Overnight work belongs to the weekday on which it begins; equal hours mean no working time.

The comparison window uses the first repeated start and second repeated end; a missing local boundary is explained. `durationMinutes`1–120 and `stepMinutes`15–120 bound actual elapsed candidate starts. Every occupied minute must fit every included participant, not just its start.

Control `includedIds`/`onIncludedIdsChange` separately from `value`/`onValueChange`, whose atomic payload is `{instant,durationMinutes,participantIds}`. Inspection is not a choice; a retained selection outside a changed context stays visible. Reset local membership explicitly with `resetKey` when the participant dataset changes. Host owns real calendars, booking and persistence.

forms-branching-survey.useWhen: Collecting conditional answers while retaining prior input when a branch changes, then reviewing the result.
forms-branching-survey.avoidWhen: A fixed linear form or automatically submitting hidden branch answers without explaining scope.
integration: Supply `formId` and up to20 unique typed `questions` (text or choice). `showWhen` refers only to a preceding question; choices are unique and bounded to12, text maximumLength1–2000. Required answers are validated before progression and submission.

Control the accepted `answers` object with `onAnswersChange`, or initialize local `defaultAnswers` and reset explicitly with `resetKey`. Earlier hidden branch answers remain in editing state but are excluded from the actual submission. Rejected requests cannot change the active branch.

Connect `onSubmit(submission,AbortSignal)` to actual persistence. The exact payload contains formId, active questionIds and copied active own answer fields only. Cancellation, changed context or handler retire stale results; failure preserves answers and review. The preview acknowledgement stores only the copied brief in preview memory.

auth-recovery-codes.useWhen: Presenting host-supplied recovery codes for explicit reveal, copying and acknowledgement.
auth-recovery-codes.avoidWhen: Generating authentication secrets in the UI or treating a copied code as proof it was stored safely.
integration: Supply stable `batchId`, `accountLabel` and up to20 unique host-issued `codes` with id, single-line code and optional used state. The named component starts empty; the default preview has visibly marked unusable examples. Used codes stay inspectable but are excluded from copied/exported/acknowledged payloads.

Clipboard success copies actual unused values and does not acknowledge storage. The user must explicitly check the saved confirmation before `onAcknowledge({batchId,codeIds},AbortSignal)`. Optional controlled `acknowledged` remains authoritative after fulfillment, with a truthful waiting state until the host updates it.

Connect explicit `onDownload`/`onPrint` handlers for copied unused-code payloads. Missing capabilities stay unavailable. One pending action, cancellation and exact set/handler/context retirement prevent obsolete receipts; errors retain supplied codes. Host owns authentication, file and print outcomes; never log codes.

forms-draft-rescue.useWhen: Resolving differences between a local draft and a newer supplied host version at field level.
forms-draft-rescue.avoidWhen: Silently overwriting a newer document or presenting a conflict that has no actual competing values.
integration: Supply up to20 unique `fields` and distinct actual `draft`/`latest` version IDs, labels and own text values (at most4000 characters per compared field). A missing field is distinct from an explicitly empty string. Only supplied comparison fields enter the resolution.

Use controlled `choices`/`onChoicesChange` or local `defaultChoices`, mapping field IDs to draft or latest. Unspecified choices keep the draft; rejected requests retain the actual accepted decisions. Individual and bulk choices remain editable until explicit resolution.

Connect `onResolve(resolution,AbortSignal)` to actual persistence. The exact payload includes both version IDs, every displayed field-source decision and merged own values. Cancellation, changed versions/choices/availability or handler retire stale completion; failure preserves both versions and decisions. The preview stores only the copied combined version in memory.

chart-sunburst-explorer.useWhen: Exploring a supplied hierarchy through radial drill-down with equivalent readable values.
chart-sunburst-explorer.avoidWhen: An unlabeled decorative ring or a hierarchy whose totals do not reconcile with its children.
integration: Supply a unique-ID hierarchy with at most 80 nodes and depth 5. Leaf values are finite nonnegative numbers up to 1 trillion; group totals are computed from their children rather than accepted as a second total. Null source and zero totals have useful native alternatives.

Control the atomic focusId/selectedId packet when the host owns the view. Selecting a real segment or its full native row inspects the same node; Focus this group and the breadcrumbs drill explicitly. Unknown identities remain unavailable, and only accepted discrete requests produce commits.

Keep exact quantities in the complete native descendant table, including tiny and zero values. Very small quantities use a truthful scientific notation. Supply the unit and supported Intl locale, and use the native controls for narrow/touch layouts.

Loading or unavailable source preserves the current packet. Live reduced motion settles the actual partition and total, idle/offscreen work stops, and actual owner-document focus fencing preserves outside and parent-page actions.

chart-sankey-paths.useWhen: Tracing supplied quantities from sources through destinations while keeping the whole flow in context.
chart-sankey-paths.avoidWhen: Invented traffic, unbalanced quantities or a diagram that can only be understood by color.
integration: Supply up to 18 unique labeled nodes in columns 0–5 and 40 unique forward links with finite nonnegative quantities up to 1 trillion. Incoming and outgoing are independent supplied-link sums; no balancing flow is invented.

Proportional ribbons support adjacent occupied stages. Empty numeric column gaps are allowed. If any connection bypasses an occupied stage, an explicit diagram fallback preserves every original category, connection and exact incoming/outgoing quantity in the native tables. Use a different graph when such bypass topology is essential.

One atomic nodeId/linkId selection chooses either a category or a connection. Emphasis traces direct links only. Rejected requests do not commit; unknown identity needs explicit clear or restored source. Full native Categories/Connections tabs provide exact quantities, units and supported Intl formatting.

Narrow actual scenes use vertical flow with full native selection targets. Geometry and figures are bounded and interruptible; live reduced motion settles their actual owners, hidden/idle work stops, and focused owner-document fences preserve native parent actions. Persistence belongs to the host.

chart-box-distribution.useWhen: Comparing the spread of a measure across a handful of groups, such as latency by region or build time by pipeline, and asking how much of each clears a limit you can drag.
chart-box-distribution.avoidWhen: Showing a single average, a trend over time, or groups with only a few observations each, where a dot plot or a plain table is more honest.
integration: Pass `groups` as { id, label, detail?, values } with raw observations, not pre-computed percentiles. Quartiles use linear interpolation and whiskers reach the furthest values inside 1.5 × IQR; the axis ends just past the slowest p99 and values beyond it are counted at the row’s edge.

Set `defaultThreshold` and `target` (0–1) to mirror your SLO, and persist changes from `onThresholdChange`, or control `threshold` yourself. Rows under target are flagged with an icon as well as colour.
Use `sort` / `onSortChange` to keep the order in sync with a table elsewhere. `showSamples` draws every observation; keep each group to a few hundred values or pass a sample for very large sets.
The limit handle is a slider: arrows move a fiftieth of an axis step, Shift moves five times that. Use `status` and `onRetry` for loading and failed fetches.

chart-calendar-heatmap.useWhen: Showing a year of daily activity at a glance, such as deploys, orders, workouts or support tickets, where weekly rhythm, quiet spells and peak days matter more than exact values.
chart-calendar-heatmap.avoidWhen: Comparing a few series, reading precise daily values, or data with fewer than a couple of months, where a bar or line chart reads faster.
integration: Pass `days` as { date, value } with ISO dates. Use `value: null` for days that weren’t measured; they render hatched and are left out of totals, streaks and averages instead of counting as zero.

Every year present in the data gets a tab. Control it with `year` and `onYearChange`, or set `defaultYear`. Days after the latest record draw as dashed outlines so a partial year still reads as a year.
Use `onSelectDate` to open a day’s detail elsewhere, or control `selectedDate`. Levels come from the quartiles of non-zero days, so a single spike doesn’t wash out the rest of the year.
Name the unit with `unit` ({ one, other }) and set `weekStart` for your locale. The accent tops a four-step ramp mixed in OKLab; pick a hue that stays distinct from your status colours.

chart-scatter-brush.useWhen: Finding and acting on a cluster of records in two measures at once, such as slow pages, expensive accounts or outlier queries, by dragging a box over them.
chart-scatter-brush.avoidWhen: Showing a trend over time, comparing a handful of categories, or plotting thousands of points where a density view or hexbin reads better.
integration: Pass `datasets` as one or more views of the same records ({ id, label, x, y }). Keep ids stable across views: points with the same id travel between them on one shared scale.
Describe each measure with `x` and `y` ({ label, unit, decimals, limit }). A limit draws a dashed guide and tints the passing quadrant; the ranked list sorts by y, highest first.
Read selections from `onBrushChange(brush, selected)` to filter a table or start a bulk action, or control `brush` yourself. Brushes are in data units, so they survive a dataset switch.

Mouse and pen brush by dragging; touch keeps page scroll and taps read the nearest point, so add `presets` for the regions people ask about most. Use `status` and `onRetry` for loading and failed fetches.

chart-funnel-dots.useWhen: Showing discrete quantities passing through stages with explicit totals and conversion denominators.
chart-funnel-dots.avoidWhen: A fabricated growth animation or percentages whose denominator changes without explanation.
integration: Supply up to 8 raw unique labeled stages in authoritative order with whole finite counts from 0 to 1 trillion. These are aggregate counts; the component does not infer matching individuals or a common cohort.

A common nice integer weight limits each stage to 80 full or partial dots. The final sector represents only the actual remainder, while native copy retains the exact count, dot weight and remainder. Actual zero has no invented dots. Quantities are not silently balanced or normalized.

Inspect one nullable host-owned stage ID with accepted-only commits. Exact ratios name both the previous supplied count and the first supplied count. Zero denominators are explicitly undefined; larger later counts can truthfully exceed 100% without claiming conversion success. Untouched loading initializes at first real ready data; explicit unknown and later chosen context remain authoritative.

Current weighted geometry and counts share bounded 320ms two-way owners with coalesced native writes when the common dot weight is unchanged. A new weight settles the matching count and geometry immediately, so the new legend never describes an old animated quantity. Live reduced motion, hidden/offscreen and blocked states settle them immediately, with no idle loop. Native stage bands stack in narrow containers, retain full labels and 44px targets, and actual document/window focus fencing preserves outside or parent actions.

data-pivot-configurator.useWhen: Letting people slice a modest dataset two ways at once, such as revenue by region and quarter, compare cells at a glance and open any cell to see the records behind it.
data-pivot-configurator.avoidWhen: Millions of rows that need server-side aggregation, or a fixed report whose grouping never changes; a plain chart or table reads faster.
integration: Describe `fields` as dimensions (with an `order` for their values) and measures (with a `format`). Pass the raw `records`; counts, sums and averages are computed locally, and an average is always taken over the records, not over group averages.

Control the grouping with `value` and `onChange`, or start uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. `columns: null` collapses the matrix to one total column. Choosing the other axis's field swaps the axes rather than duplicating one.
Use `onCellSelect` to open the records behind a cell in your own drawer or list; the built-in inspector shows the six largest. Cells are buttons with arrow-key navigation.
Keep matrices small enough to read (four to six values per axis). Turn off `heatmap` when the values aren't comparable, and set `disabled` for read-only dashboards where cells should still open.

data-column-workbench.useWhen: Letting people rearrange a dense operational table in place: drag columns into a new order, freeze the identifying ones on the left, hide the noise and set widths.
data-column-workbench.avoidWhen: Choosing which records to show (that is filtering) or editing cell values; this changes the view of a table, not its data.
integration: Pass `columns` and `rows`; each row's `cells` is keyed by column id and rendered as text, mono, right-aligned numbers or a status with a dot from `tones`. Mark identifier columns `required` so they can't be hidden.

Store the arrangement from `onChange(value, change)`: an ordered `{ id, visible, pinned, width }` array, one entry per column. Drags and resizes report once, on release, so it is safe to save each change to a saved view.
Use `value` to restore a saved layout or `defaultValue` to start uncontrolled. Unknown ids are dropped and missing columns are appended, so a layout saved before you add a column still loads.

Every action has a keyboard path: grips move with the arrow keys, Home and End, and resize handles take arrow keys. Set `disabled` for viewers who may read but not rearrange, and `density="compact"` for long tables.

data-bulk-action-review.useWhen: Running one action over many records where the scope must be seen before it is confirmed, some records can't take the action, and some may fail.
data-bulk-action-review.avoidWhen: A single-record action, or a reversible bulk edit where an undo toast is kinder than a review step.
integration: Pass `records` with `heldReason` on any the action can't touch (an owner, a directory-managed account); they join a held-back pile instead of the action. Give each an `impact` line so the review says exactly what happens to it.
Control `selectedIds` with `onSelectionChange`. The array keeps pick order, which is the stack order. Nothing is selected implicitly; select-all is an explicit checkbox.

`onApply(ids)` receives only the eligible ids and resolves with `{ id, ok, message? }` per record. Failed records stay with their message; rejecting means nothing ran and the review stays open. The scope is frozen at review time, so you can remove finished rows from `records` as soon as the request returns.

Word the action with `action` and `noun`, and use `summarize` for the consequence that matters (seats freed, refund total). Retry reopens a review of just the failures; `onDone(failedIds)` fires when the receipt is dismissed.

data-filter-history.useWhen: Letting people rewind a filtered table through its saved filter states, see exactly which rows each state brings back or drops, and restore one deliberately.
data-filter-history.avoidWhen: Building a filter from scratch, or keeping a long audit log of every edit; this shows a handful of saved states, not a version-control system.
integration: Pass `fields`, `records` and `history` (oldest first). Each snapshot is a full rule set `{ fieldId, operator, value }` with `is`, `is_not`, `contains`, `gte` and `lte`. Counts and rows are computed locally from the records you pass, so send the same rows the live table shows.

Control the live rules with `value` and `onValueChange(rules, snapshotId)`, or start uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. Scrubbing only changes the preview; the host's rules change only when someone presses Restore, and the callback receives a copy.
Add `onRename(id, name)` to enable inline naming. Return a promise for a pending state; reject to keep the draft open with an error, and update `history` with the new name when it succeeds.

Set `defaultSnapshotId` to open on a past state, `showDiff={false}` to hide live rows a snapshot would drop, and `disabled` for read-only viewers who can still scrub. Use `recordLabel` and `noun` to rename the first column and the count for your data.

editor-layer-stack.useWhen: Reordering, locking, hiding and renaming supplied layers with actual selection and a readable move mode.
editor-layer-stack.avoidWhen: A complete drawing canvas or visual layers that have no corresponding host objects.
integration: Supply controlled `value`/`onValueChange` or local `defaultValue` as a flat ordered array of up to64 unique actual layer records. Each has id, name, kind, visible and locked fields. Groups are flat host records; the component does not invent a drawing canvas or tree.

Control inspection separately with `selectedId`/`onSelectedIdChange`, or use local `defaultSelectedId`. Locked layers remain inspectable and can be shown/hidden or unlocked, while direct moving/renaming is unavailable. Native dragging has cancel/context retirement; move buttons and Alt+Up/Down offer equivalent ordering.

Explicit Apply requests cloned stack state. Rejected edits retain accepted order and newer rename drafts through older acknowledgements. Availability or lock changes retain a read-only name draft for recovery. Local deletion selects an actual neighbor; a missing controlled selection stays explicit. Use `resetKey` for an explicit new editing lifecycle.

editor-color-token-studio.useWhen: Editing semantic color tokens and checking actual supplied foreground/background contrast pairs.
editor-color-token-studio.avoidWhen: Claiming accessibility for an entire application from a few colors or generating an arbitrary decorative palette.
integration: Supply controlled `value`/`onValueChange` or local `defaultValue` with up to24 unique CSS-safe semantic token IDs. Complete RGB/RGBA hexadecimal drafts preview separately from accepted token values; Apply requests a copied palette and old acknowledgement cannot discard newer hex text.

Provide up to32 actual `pairs` referencing token IDs with fontSize/fontWeight. Contrast composites foreground over background over opaque `canvasColor`, then uses unrounded sRGB luminance and WCAG text thresholds. Missing or unsupported colors/references are explicit; an incomplete draft leaves the accepted reading palette visible. [WCAG contrast reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html).

Use supplied `presets` as draft suggestions and `sampleText` as actual reading content. Export `scopeSelector` supports :root, a simple class/ID or a simple data-attribute equality selector. Copy exports only complete accepted CSS, acknowledges the real Clipboard API result and fences stale receipts to exact bytes. The full accepted CSS stays selectable after clipboard failure.

editor-spacing-inspector.useWhen: Inspecting and changing real padding and gap on supplied content, with measurements from the rendered CSS box.
editor-spacing-inspector.avoidWhen: A full page-layout engine or measurement of intrinsic artwork outside the supplied box.
integration: Supply bounded integer SpacingValue padding0–96/gap0–64 and row/column direction. Linked editing requests all four edges atomically; gap remains independent.
Provide value and onValueChange for controlled accepted spacing. Incomplete numeric buffers and newer drafts remain separate from accepted layout; synchronous failures preserve the actual layout.
Measurements use logical computed CSS pixels, including animated padding/gap and independently scaled axes. Export contains accepted flex/padding/gap CSS; Clipboard failure leaves selectable output.

editor-branch-compare.useWhen: Choosing individual additions, removals, text and parent changes between two actual document structures.
editor-branch-compare.avoidWhen: A language-aware source-code merge, unbounded document parser or automatic persistence engine.
integration: Supply distinct current/incoming version identities and up to48 unique acyclic nodes each, depth at most6, with actual parent identity, body and bounded sibling order.

Controlled decisions reference unique changed nodes. Unspecified nodes retain current; choosing an absent source explicitly omits it. A mixed structure with missing parents or cycles remains unavailable.

onApply receives both exact version IDs, cloned complete merged nodes and copied complete changed-node decisions plus AbortSignal. Awaiting fulfillment acknowledges the request only; your host supplies the persisted versions. Changed source facts, including in-place mutations, retire stale acknowledgment.

editor-asset-license-sheet.useWhen: Reviewing actual asset provenance and host-supplied usage eligibility for a specific project before selecting an asset.
editor-asset-license-sheet.avoidWhen: Interpreting a third-party licence or granting rights from a visual component.
integration: Supply exact project identity/title/usage and up to32 unique asset records with actual creator/source, terms and boolean-or-null project eligibility. Unknown eligibility stays unavailable.

Eligible assets need supplied terms and explicit review. If the host requires a credit, supply and review that exact credit. Availability interruptions preserve review; changed selected asset/project facts retire it.

onSelect receives a copied exact project, asset/all terms and review snapshot with AbortSignal. Fulfillment acknowledges only selection request; host owns rights evaluation, persistence and project attachment.

editor-storyboard-strip.useWhen: Planning a short film, ad or product video as a sequence of shots, where people reorder shots by drag, trim their lengths and need the cut to land on a target duration.
editor-storyboard-strip.avoidWhen: Frame-accurate editing of real footage, multi-track timelines with audio, or slide decks where items have no duration.
integration: Supply scenes as { id, title, notes, duration, shot, tone, thumbnail }. Pass a real frame URL as thumbnail when you have one; otherwise the board is drawn from the shot type and its two tone colours.
Durations snap to half seconds between 0.5 and 20. Set targetDuration to the length the cut must hit; the meter and readout show the time to spare or the overrun.
onScenesChange receives the full ordered list after each finished change: a drag dropped, an Earlier or Later move, a trim released or a stepper press. Store it as the new order and lengths.

editor-keyframe-track.useWhen: Editing a short UI or motion-design animation by keyframes, where people scrub a playhead, watch a live preview and drag keys in time and value on a curve.
editor-keyframe-track.avoidWhen: Long video timelines with clips and audio, physics or spring authoring, or animations defined entirely in code with no visual tuning.
integration: Give tracks as { id, label, unit, min, max, step, keys } with keys in frame order; each key's ease (linear, ease or hold) shapes the segment that leaves it. Keys never cross or share a frame.

renderPreview(values) receives the current value of every track by id; draw your own component with them. valueAt(track, frame) is exported so your runtime and tests evaluate tracks exactly as the editor does.
onChange(tracks) fires after finished edits only (a drag released, a stepper commit, a key added, re-eased or deleted), so it is safe to persist or push to an undo stack.

editor-version-restore.useWhen: Letting writers browse the saved versions of a document, compare any version with the live text word by word, and restore all of it or only chosen blocks with an undo.
editor-version-restore.avoidWhen: Code review diffs, merge conflict resolution between branches, or audit logs where versions are read but never restored.
integration: Describe the document as ordered blocks ({ id, kind, label }) and give each version text per block id. A block missing from a version reads as not in that version and cannot be restored on its own.
Pass versions newest first. Name the milestones (Copy edit, Legal review) and leave autosaves unnamed; the timeline and the grouped list are built from day and time.

onRestore receives { versionId, blockIds, content }. Persist it and resolve; the component updates the live text, adds a Before restore entry and offers Undo, which calls onUndo with the same request. Reject with an Error to show its message; the ticked blocks stay ticked.

editor-export-preset.useWhen: Exporting a frame, card or layer from a design or content tool, where people pick an artboard size, format, scale and quality and want to see the result and its file size before writing it.
editor-export-preset.avoidWhen: Batch exports of many assets at once, server-side render queues, or a plain download button with no settings to choose.
integration: Pass your own artwork and its background as React nodes. The frame is a size container, so size the artwork in cqw, cqh and cqmin and it reflows to every artboard; the background fades out for transparent exports.

Supply presets as { id, label, width, height, note } and restrict formats to the ones your renderer writes. estimateExportBytes and formatBytes are exported if you show the same figure elsewhere; replace them with your encoder's real numbers when you have them.

onExport receives { presetId, width, height, scale, format, quality, transparent, fileName, estimatedBytes } with the scale already applied. Resolve when the file is written; reject with an Error whose message the panel shows, and every setting stays as it was for a retry.

editor-font-pairing.useWhen: Pairing actual host font roles against supplied copy before applying typography and copying accepted CSS.
editor-font-pairing.avoidWhen: An automatic font downloader or guessed font-availability detector.
integration: Supply up to16 unique PairingFont records with actual role/optional family, supported weights and ready/loading/unavailable/unknown readiness. The host owns assets/loading. Unready fonts show the explicit standard role fallback and cannot be copied or applied as ready.
Supply actual headingText/bodyText and accepted heading/body identities, weights, sizes24–96/12–24px and body lineHeight1.2–2.2. Actual draft font-size/leading transitions respect reduced motion.

Use value/onValueChange for copied accepted typography. Rejected/older acknowledgments retain newer drafts. Clipboard copies exact accepted CSS, with selectable failure fallback and stale-result fencing when actual font/settings facts change.

ai-context-budget.useWhen: Reviewing supplied context sources and their real token allocation against a bounded model budget.
ai-context-budget.avoidWhen: Guessing token counts or treating a visual budget as authority to read private sources.
integration: Supply stable context-source identities, kind, required/unavailable state and actual token counts. A null count remains unknown. Required sources count toward the limit and cannot be silently removed; reserved tokens remain explicit.

Control included IDs through value/onValueChange, with inspection separate from inclusion. Changed budgets never silently prune selected sources. This planner neither fetches source content nor runs an AI request.

ai-answer-compare.useWhen: Comparing supplied responses to the same request with their evidence and an explicit preference.
ai-answer-compare.avoidWhen: Generating answers, assuming a model is better without evidence or silently applying an inspected response.
integration: Supply the shared request, stable response/section identities, actual content and evidence. Unknown evidence IDs and unavailable responses remain explicit; no model score or generated answer is inferred.

Treat preference as an explicit acknowledged host decision. Request-content changes and reset identity retire pending work even when response IDs are reused; controlled values remain authoritative and rejected preferences preserve reading positions.

ai-structured-output.useWhen: Inspecting supplied structured fields as they become complete, valid or invalid during an actual stream.
ai-structured-output.avoidWhen: Inventing completed values, hiding validation failures or claiming to execute a schema-driven workflow.
integration: Supply stable fields with actual path, declared JSON type (string, number, boolean, null, object or array), value, waiting/partial/valid/invalid/unavailable state and meaningful messages. outputState/outputMessage describes actual host streaming/completion/failure; rawOutput is received text, not invented validated JSON.

Selection is an exact value/defaultValue/onValueChange ID contract; inspection filters are local. Only unique, valid, type-matching, finite, acyclic and bounded field values can be copied as validated output. Explicit raw copying keeps the received state clear.

Real onRetry(field, AbortSignal) and field clipboard jobs are owned by exact field content/state and unique identity, output/reset scope, availability and callback identity. A newly duplicated active ID aborts recovery and retires field-copy receipts; old settlement cannot affect corrected newer work. Raw-text copying keeps its independent supplied-text scope. Missing handlers never show fake recovery controls.

Optional defaultView starts named inspection in field or raw mode and reapplies on resetKey. The original demo begins with a complete raw payload derived only from its own fields; caller fields receive no unrelated stand-in. Raw copying remains explicitly separate from validated field output.

agents-dependency-board.useWhen: Inspecting supplied task dependencies and tracing actual blockers with a readable graph and linear alternative.
agents-dependency-board.avoidWhen: A general node editor, invented agent activity or treating a circular dependency as a runnable plan.
integration: Supply stable task IDs, raw dependency arrays and actual queued/running/blocked/complete/error statuses. Distinguish missing nodes, cycles and repeated IDs. A dependency with conflicting supplied records is ambiguous even when its first visual variant is complete; keep all raw variants inspectable.

Selection is controlled/uncontrolled, while graph/list and dependency/dependent tracing are local inspection. Preserve actual selection through status updates and use resetKey for a replacement plan. Keyboard focus reveals complete targets inside the bounded local graph/list.

This board does not execute tasks or infer permission from a valid graph. Local inspection is bounded to 200 unique tasks and 60 graph cards; expose incomplete or out-of-bound relationships rather than treating omitted data as complete.

agents-run-replay.useWhen: Reconstructing visible state from a supplied event history while scrubbing a completed or partial run.
agents-run-replay.avoidWhen: Executing agent tools, generating an event history or presenting replayed actions as current live activity.
integration: Supply unique event IDs, nonnegative safe whole-millisecond timestamps and complete snapshots. The clock selects only the last supplied snapshot at or before it; equal-time events preserve order and explicit inspection can pin one actual snapshot. No intermediate workflow state is inferred.

Pair controlled time with synchronous onTimeChange. Accepted conventional inline observers may change reference without retiring the same-history clock owner. A rejected playback request stops; removing the required observer makes the controlled clock read-only. Exact entry preserves dirty drafts and later typing through older acknowledgements.

User-started 1x/2x playback executes nothing and stops for history/reset replacement, explicit seek, hidden/offscreen/window blur, rejection or unmount. Live reduced motion stops decorative tweens while preserving meaningful explicit clock playback. Invalid/duplicate records remain inspectable and cannot drive playback.

agents-budget-guard.useWhen: Reviewing supplied estimated and actual usage against limits before explicitly authorizing a bounded action.
agents-budget-guard.avoidWhen: Inventing costs, automatically approving an action or describing an estimate as the final charge.
integration: Supply exact action and independent token/call/cost budgets. Estimate is the host prospective total in its scope, not an amount the component adds to actual. Missing pre-action actual is Not measured yet; missing limits/estimates, explicit null/nonfinite data, duplicate IDs and unsupported currencies/scales block authorization.

Review consent belongs to the exact action and material budget data; replacement retires it permanently. Keep newer notes through bounds/status/error/cancel, and use resetKey for explicit lifecycle reset. Pass the exact reviewed snapshot and note to the real onAuthorize(payload, AbortSignal).

Pending, rejection, cancellation and late acknowledgements are owned by exact content/callback/availability. Fulfilment alone shows Awaiting action status and blocks duplicate authorization; only supplied authoritative status can mark authorization, execution or completion. Monetary minor units use exact BigInt formatting and remain separate across currencies.

devtools-release-compare.useWhen: Comparing supplied deployments and their changed resources before a reviewed host-owned rollback request.
devtools-release-compare.avoidWhen: Performing an implicit deployment or claiming a rollback succeeded without an actual host result.
integration: Supply immutable current/candidate releases with ID, label, supported timestamp, resourcesComplete and actual resource ID/path/kind/bytes/digest/text. Equal size alone is unverified; complete opposite inventory is required to call a resource added or removed. Raw identity conflicts stay visible.

Pair target value with onValueChange for controlled inspection. Review requests require an earlier supported target, complete unique inventories and known content comparisons. Consent belongs to the exact current/target manifest pair and retires permanently on replacement; byte subtotals stay exact and unknown sizes remain separate.

Pass the copied reviewed pair to onRequestRollback(review, AbortSignal), preserve context through failure/cancel and fence old results by target/content/callback/reset ownership. Acknowledgement shows Awaiting current release, blocks duplicate requests and never invents a deployment change; only the supplied current release reports deployment.

devtools-request-replay.useWhen: Editing a supplied request and inspecting the response returned by a real host request handler.
devtools-request-replay.avoidWhen: Pretending a demonstration payload came from a live server or sending a request without an explicit action.
integration: Supply request/defaultRequest with stable ID, supported HTTP method, HTTP(S) or root-relative URL, lossless header rows and text body. Pair controlled request with synchronous onRequestChange; without it, editing is read-only. Apply submits an exact draft while rejected controlled edits remain retained.

onReplay receives only the accepted applied snapshot and AbortSignal. The handler owns networking, authentication and CORS and returns actual HTTP status, header rows, body and optional measured elapsedMs. A void acknowledgement never fabricates a response or timing. Keep each returned exchange visibly paired to its exact sent request.

Pending typing stays a newer draft. Accepted request/content/session/handler replacement or unmount retires old jobs; cancel and newer-job/old-finally are fenced. Preserve the last response with an earlier-request label after changed input or failure. Native copying belongs to the actual returned body and bounded/truncated data is never copied as complete.

devtools-schema-migration.useWhen: Reviewing a supplied schema migration plan, its dependencies and actual impact before requesting application.
devtools-schema-migration.avoidWhen: Executing arbitrary SQL in the component or inventing the migration’s safety, backups or success.
integration: Supply plan identity, complete ordered inventory and change ID/title/operation/resource/statement/dependencyIds/impact. Keep row impact per change; overlapping counts are not a unique total. Missing, repeated, cyclic, later or ambiguous dependencies and unknown affected-row/lock/reversible facts block reviewed application.
