Pair selected change value with onValueChange for controlled inspection. Statements and the full raw plan remain selectable escaped text; this component does not execute SQL. Exact consent belongs to plan facts, order, impact, status and handler and cannot resurrect after replacement. Later notes stay drafts while pending requests keep their exact copied note.

onApply receives a copied plan/note plus AbortSignal. Preserve context on failure/cancel and fence obsolete plan/session/handler/terminal ownership. Same-plan applying progress does not self-abort the real handler. Void acknowledgement shows Awaiting host status and blocks duplicate requests; only actual supplied status can report Applied.

devtools-incident-timeline.useWhen: Correlating supplied alerts, deployments and interventions on one inspectable incident history.
devtools-incident-timeline.avoidWhen: A live monitoring service or assumed causal relationships between nearby events.
integration: Supply incident identity and actual event ID, explicit supported ISO timestamp, alert/deployment/intervention/note category, description, actor and event-scoped evidence. Equal times preserve supplied order. Missing/conflicting IDs and unsupported kinds/times remain inspectable as unplaced raw records; bound inspection explicitly rather than silently legitimizing a record.

Pair event value and timeZone with their respective synchronous observers for controlled inspection. Missing observers make only that branch read-only. Display-zone conversion uses actual IANA rules while retaining source timestamps; unavailable conversion shows raw times. Time-zone option IDs must be supported and unique.

Category filters keep the inspected event/evidence in view and explain when its row is hidden. Evidence identity includes event ID and local evidence ID; actual supplied HTTP(S) or root-relative links remain available, while missing/unsupported links stay honest. Use incident/resetKey to replace history and preserve explicit outside or parent-page focus.

This is history inspection, not monitoring, causal analysis or assumed recovery. Fixed row spacing is not a time scale and temporal proximity does not establish cause. Inspection is bounded to 200 supported records before chronological ordering and 100 evidence records per event; the host retains complete data.

mobile-mood-map.useWhen: A wellbeing or journaling app needs a quick, expressive self-reported check-in: people place how they feel on an energy × pleasantness map and log it against their day.
mobile-mood-map.avoidWhen: You need clinical scales (PHQ-9, GAD-7), free-text sentiment detection, or a mood picker so small that a row of chips would do.
integration: Supply your own `feelings` with pleasantness and energy from −1 to 1; the colour of each is blended from the four `colors`, so keep those as your brand's data palette.

Pass today's earlier check-ins as `log` and the current time as `nowMinute`; `onSave` receives { feeling, note, minute } with an AbortSignal and should reject on failure so the retry state appears with the note intact.
Control the selection with `value` and `onValueChange` to sync it with a store; the callback fires when a drag settles, not on every frame.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify the drag, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-habit-grid.useWhen: A wellbeing, fitness or productivity app shows this week's habits at a glance and lets people mark any day so far with one tap, with streaks and a weekly target.
mobile-habit-grid.avoidWhen: You need long-range history (months or a year heatmap), habits measured in amounts rather than done or not done, or a single habit's detail view.
integration: Pass `habits` ({ id, name, icon, target, streak, paused }), the seven `days` and `todayIndex`; days after today are disabled.

Keep marks in your store with `value` and `onValueChange(next, change)`, and persist through `onToggle(change, signal)`: the cell fills at once, and a rejection rolls it back with a shake and a retry note.
`streak` is the run before today; the component adds today's mark, so send the server's figure rather than recomputing it on the client.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify touch, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-focus-session.useWhen: A single focus or pomodoro session on a phone: set the length on a dial, watch the time run down, pause or finish, and log the minutes against a daily goal.
mobile-focus-session.avoidWhen: Scheduling a day of tasks, tracking habits over weeks, or a background timer that must keep running and notify while the app is closed.
integration: The component runs its own clock from wall time, so it survives dropped frames. Use initialPhase and defaultElapsedSeconds to resume a session in progress, and phase to drive it from outside (a change plays like a tap).

onPhaseChange reports ready, running, paused and finished; onComplete receives { intention, plannedMinutes, focusedMinutes, completed } once per session. Persist it and pass the day's sessions back as completedToday.

presets, defaultMinutes and maxMinutes (one turn of the dial) set the lengths; dailyGoalMinutes sets the goal track. defaultDoNotDisturb and onDoNotDisturbChange wire the moon button to your own focus mode.

accent recolours the arc, its head and the live segment. Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once); background timing and notifications belong to the host.

mobile-day-planner.useWhen: A calendar, planner or focus app shows one day as a timeline and lets people move an event by dragging it, with clashes flagged and an explicit confirm before the calendar changes.
mobile-day-planner.avoidWhen: You need a week or month grid, multi-day or all-day events, creating events by dragging on empty time, or several people's calendars side by side.
integration: Pass `events` with `startMinute` and `endMinute` in local minutes after midnight; set `editable: false` with an `unavailableReason` for events the person doesn't own.

`onReschedule({ event, startMinute, endMinute, conflicts }, signal)` runs when Move is pressed; resolve once your calendar accepts it, reject to keep the proposal on screen with a retry. Send the updated `events` afterwards.
Set `dayStart`, `dayEnd` and `minuteStep` to your product's working day and grid; leave `nowMinute` out on days other than today. `allowOverlap` decides whether a clash can be confirmed.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify the drag, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-journal-prompt.useWhen: A journaling, therapy-adjacent or wellbeing app offers a few reflection prompts and a calm place to answer them, with drafts that survive switching prompts and an explicit keep.
mobile-journal-prompt.avoidWhen: You need long-form documents with formatting, a feed of past entries, or free writing with no prompts; a plain editor or list fits better.
integration: Pass `prompts` ({ id, title, question, guidance }) and the answers already kept as `answers` ({ promptId, text, updatedLabel }); kept prompts show a chip on their card.

`onSave({ prompt, text, previous }, signal)` runs when the person keeps an answer. Resolve once it's stored; reject to show the error with the words untouched. Pass `timeLabel` so the stamp matches your clock.
Control the current prompt with `selectedId` and `onSelectionChange` if your app deep-links to one; `streak` and `wordGoal` come from your own data and never block keeping.
Install this in a React Native app (run npx install-expo-modules once in bare projects). The web preview is a review surface; verify the keyboard, text scaling and screen readers on devices.

mobile-reading-progress.useWhen: An e-reader or audiobook library screen showing how far someone is through a book, its chapters and saved pages, with one tap back into reading.
mobile-reading-progress.avoidWhen: Rendering the book itself, or tracking reading goals and streaks across many books.
integration: Supply the book (id, title, author, pages, cover colours), chapters with first pages, and currentPage. Bookmarks can be controlled (bookmarks + onBookmarksChange) or local (defaultBookmarks).
onResume({ bookId, chapterId, page }, signal) opens your reader at the chosen page: the reader's place, or wherever the page edge, a chapter or a bookmark pointed. Jumping never marks pages as read.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once. Verify the page-edge drag, larger text and assistive technology on target devices.

mobile-trip-itinerary.useWhen: A trip with several legs across time zones, where travellers need local times, delays and cancellations at a glance and a quick way into each booking.
mobile-trip-itinerary.avoidWhen: Searching or booking travel, live vehicle tracking, or a single flight's status card.
integration: Supply legs in travel order with ISO instants (with an offset or Z), an IANA timeZone, code, city and lat/lon per place, a status, optional revised times, the operator's note and booking details. Clocks and day headers are formatted in each place's own zone.

onOpenLeg(leg, signal) opens the boarding pass, ticket or ride in your app; Cancel aborts the signal and late answers to older requests are ignored. Pass now to decide the next leg; tightConnection flags short connections.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once. Verify scrolling, larger text and assistive technology on target devices.

mobile-packing-list.useWhen: A travel or kit checklist where weight matters, so people see a bag fill toward a limit as they pack and adjust quantities to stay under it.
mobile-packing-list.avoidWhen: A general to-do list with no notion of weight or capacity, or inventory that needs search, sorting and bulk editing.
integration: Pass `trip` as { destination, dates, bag, limitKg, tareKg } and `items` as { id, name, detail?, group, qty, grams, packed }. Sections follow the order groups first appear; the bag's own weight counts from the start.
`onChange(items, change)` fires on pack, unpack, quantity, remove and restore with the whole list. It can return a promise; reject or throw and the list rolls back with your message in the toast.
Over the limit the bag and weight turn red regardless of `accent`. Remove offers Undo, which restores the item to its place.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg. Check the checkbox targets, the stepper with VoiceOver and larger text on devices.

mobile-budget-envelope.useWhen: Letting someone move money between budget categories on a phone, with the month's unassigned balance updating as they drag and nothing saved until the host accepts.
mobile-budget-envelope.avoidWhen: Moving real money between accounts, showing transaction history or charts of past spending, or a budget that isn't zero-based.
integration: envelopes: { id, name, icon, budgeted, spent, lastPeriod? } with icons home, basket, fork, car, bolt, coins, ticket or gift. Pass a new array to replace what the screen has accepted; income minus the budgets is Ready to Assign.

onBudgetChange(change) receives { envelopeId, name, from, to, readyToAssign }. Resolve to accept (the row and hero count to the new value); reject or throw and the sheet keeps the draft, shakes once and offers a retry.
step sets the ruler's notch; typed amounts keep their cents. allowOverAssign lets a budget exceed what's ready to assign; otherwise the ruler rubber-bands at the limit and says why.

openId and onOpenChange drive the envelope sheet from outside (null or an unknown id closes it). accent recolours the open segment, the needle and a balanced month; red is reserved for overspent and over-assigned.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once). Check real devices for keyboard, large text and assistive technology.

mobile-voice-memo.useWhen: Playing back a recorded memo, interview or voice note where people scrub by dragging the waveform, jump between markers and read along with a timed transcript.
mobile-voice-memo.avoidWhen: Recording audio, editing or trimming a clip, or a music player with queues and artwork; use a now-playing screen for music.
integration: Supply measured peaks (0–1, evenly spaced, about six a second), markers and transcript sentences with start and end seconds. Without a transcript the screen shows a written empty state.

The screen runs the playhead clock. Mirror it into your audio engine with onPlayingChange(playing, position), onSeek(position) and onRateChange(rate); onMarkerAdd reports markers dropped at the playhead.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once for expo-blur and expo-linear-gradient. Verify gestures, larger text and assistive technology on target devices.

mobile-project-switcher.useWhen: Apps where people work across several projects or workspaces and switch often, and the project's home should change around them without a page load.
mobile-project-switcher.avoidWhen: Apps with a single workspace, switching accounts or organisations with separate sign-ins, or very long lists that need a full search screen.
integration: Pass `projects` with stable ids, a glyph, the figures the home shows (open issues, cycle, seven days of activity, recent items) and `locked` with the reason for projects the person can't open.

Control `value` and resolve `onValueChange(id, project)` once your session has switched; reject with an Error to keep the current project and show the message on its row. Use `open` and `onOpenChange` to drive the sheet, and `onRequestAccess` for locked rows.

Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (`npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps). The mark's flight measures on-screen positions, so test inside your navigation container on devices.

mobile-file-preview.useWhen: Reading a shared document on a phone before acting on it: skimming pages, jumping to the one with comments, then downloading or opening it elsewhere.
mobile-file-preview.avoidWhen: Editing documents, browsing a folder of many files, or previewing images and video where a media viewer fits better.
integration: Pass `file` metadata and a `renderPage(index, width)` that draws each page with your PDF or document renderer; heights follow A-series proportions (width × 1.414). Mark commented pages with `marks`.
Drive `status` from your renderer: loading, ready, unsupported or error, with `statusMessage` for specifics and `onRetry` for the error panel.

Implement `onDownload(file, report)` and call `report(fraction)` as bytes arrive; reject with an Error to show its message. Wire `onOpen`, `onShare` and `onBack`. Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (`npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps).

mobile-attachment-tray.useWhen: Picking several files to send into a conversation on a phone, with real previews, a visible size limit, uploads that finish in place and a send that lands as one message.
mobile-attachment-tray.avoidWhen: Browsing a whole file system, previewing a single document full screen, or sending files outside a conversation.
integration: files are TrayFile { id, name, kind, bytes, status?, progress?, detail?, reason? }. Update status and progress from your uploader; only ready files can be picked. Failed files show their reason and call onRetry(file) when tapped.
maxFiles and maxBytes are enforced where the pick happens: a refused tile shakes and the hint explains. The meter shows the running total against the limit.
onSend({ files, note, totalBytes }) sends the selection. Resolve and the tiles leave, the tray folds and a message lands in the thread; reject and the files and note stay with an error.

renderThumbnail(file) draws a real preview (an Image) in place of the bundled drawings. messages and recipient set the conversation behind the tray; tray and onTrayChange drive it from outside; onAdd shows a Browse button for your picker.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once). Check the keyboard with the growing note field on real devices.

mobile-meeting-preflight.useWhen: The moment before joining a video call: checking your camera, microphone and speaker, choosing devices and joining once you're ready.
mobile-meeting-preflight.avoidWhen: The in-call screen itself, scheduling meetings, or apps without camera or microphone access.
integration: Pass your camera view as preview and subscribe the mic meter with micLevel(emit), returning an unsubscribe. Supply devices per group with availability, and readiness checks; a blocked check disables Join and says why.

onJoin({ roomId, muted, cameraOn, backgroundBlur, devices }, signal) joins the room; resolve when you're in. Cancel aborts the signal, and a rejection keeps every setting and offers Retry. Device, mute, camera and blur changes are reported through their callbacks.
Install in a React Native app; bare apps run npx install-expo-modules once. Request camera and microphone permissions in your app before showing this screen, and verify on target devices.

mobile-channel-thread.useWhen: Reading and replying to one threaded conversation in a team channel on a phone, with quoting, reactions and honest sending, sent and failed states for your reply.
mobile-channel-thread.avoidWhen: A one-to-one chat with bubbles, a channel's full message list, or a transport layer that needs delivery receipts from other people.
integration: root and replies are ThreadMessage { id, author, time, text, quoteId?, reactions?, attachment? }. A reply with quoteId shows the quoted reply above its text.
onSend({ text, quoteId }) posts a reply. It appears at once as Sending; resolve to mark it Sent; reject and it stays as Not sent with a tap to retry, so the text is never lost.
status drives the thread: loading shows placeholder rows, error shows a banner over the cached replies with Retry (onRetry), unavailable makes the composer read-only with statusMessage in your words.
onReact(messageId, kind, mine) reports reaction toggles (check, eyes, heart); counts update immediately. accent recolours the send button, your reactions and the quote you are replying to.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare React Native: npx install-expo-modules once). Verify keyboard avoidance and safe areas in the host app.

mobile-task-move.useWhen: Changing an issue's status on a phone where the workflow has rules: work-in-progress limits, columns that need approval, and a move that should be easy to take back.
mobile-task-move.avoidWhen: Rearranging many cards across a full board, free-form kanban with no workflow rules, or desktop drag-and-drop between columns.
integration: Pass `task` and the ordered `statuses` for its workflow. Give each column a `kind` so the glyph shows progress, a `count`, an optional `limit` and a `blockedReason` for rules the server enforces.

Implement `onMove({ task, from, to, note })` against your tracker and throw an Error with a readable message to refuse; the note is kept. `onUndo` is offered for `undoSeconds` after a successful move.

Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (`npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps), and check the puck drag inside your own scroll views and with VoiceOver's adjustable actions.

mobile-review-annotations.useWhen: Reviewing a still image or design on a phone, where comments are pinned to exact points, reviewers resolve them one by one and can drop a new pin by tapping the artwork.
mobile-review-annotations.avoidWhen: Reviewing video or multi-page documents, or threaded discussions that need full reply chains on screen.
integration: Pass the image as `artwork` (any element that fills its box) with its `aspectRatio`, and `annotations` as { id, x, y, author, initials, text, time, replies?, resolved? }, where x and y are the pin tip from 0 to 1 across the artwork.

`onResolve(id, resolved)` is optimistic and rolls back if it rejects. `onAdd({ x, y, text })` can resolve with the saved annotation to replace the local one; reject and the draft stays with your error.
Tapping a pin zooms to it and swiping the cards moves the camera; `defaultSelectedId` picks the first comment shown.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg. Test pin tap targets, the carousel with VoiceOver and the composer with the keyboard open on devices.

mobile-notification-digest.useWhen: A scheduled summary of notifications grouped by app, where people clear the backlog by swiping each one to read or snooze it and expect a quick Undo.
mobile-notification-digest.avoidWhen: A live notification feed that must show each push as it arrives, or an inbox where messages are opened and replied to in place.
integration: Pass `groups` as { id, app, icon, items } with items { id, title, body, time, timeSensitive? }. Icons are drawn monochrome glyphs: tasks, chat, calendar, bank, transit and parcel.

Reads and snoozes are optimistic. `onRead` and `onSnooze` (with the chosen { id, label, until } option) can return a promise; reject or throw and the notification comes back with your message in the toast. `onRestore` fires on Undo.
`defaultExpanded` opens one pile on first view; `nextSummary` sets the caught-up message.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg. The cards are glass over a drawn wallpaper; keep something with luminance behind them if you change the background.

mobile-sync-conflict.useWhen: Resolving a record that two people or devices edited offline, field by field, where each person should see both versions and physically pick one before the merge is saved.
mobile-sync-conflict.avoidWhen: Automatic last-write-wins sync, text documents that need a character-level merge, or conflicts with more than two versions of a field.
integration: Pass the two sides as `mine` and `theirs` ({ name, initials, device, deviceName, editedAt }), the conflicting fields as { id, label, mine, theirs } and any agreed fields as `settled` for context. Changed words are highlighted from a word diff of the two values.
Each card can be dragged over the other or kept with its button. `onChoose` reports every choice with { fieldId, choice, value } so you can keep a draft; `defaultChoices` resumes one.
`onSave` receives every resolution once all fields are chosen. Resolve to show the synced state; reject or throw to keep the choices and show your error message with a retry.
Install expo-blur, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg (bare apps run `npx install-expo-modules`). Check drag, VoiceOver and large text on devices.

mobile-offline-outbox.useWhen: A mobile app that saves work without signal and needs one place to see what is waiting, send it on demand and fix the changes a server turns down.
mobile-offline-outbox.avoidWhen: Apps that are always online, background sync you never surface to people, or resolving rich merge conflicts field by field.
integration: Supply `items` from your local queue with stable ids, a kind, size and saved time. Pass `network` from your connectivity listener: Wi-Fi drains automatically, mobile data waits for Send now, offline waits.

Implement `onSend` to apply one change and throw an Error with a readable message when the server rejects it; the message is shown on the row and in the sheet, and the change stays queued. Edited notes arrive with their new `body`.

Remove discarded changes in `onDiscard`. Install `expo-blur`, `expo-linear-gradient` and `react-native-svg` (run `npx install-expo-modules` once in bare apps) and verify on devices with real connectivity changes.
